anomalies.observed: On thermocouples.kicad_sch the middle MAX31855 (U8) has its ~{CS} pin (pin 6) tied to net NET0015 — the same net as its SO/MISO output (pin 7) and the SO outputs of the other two MAX31855s (U11, U10). All three SO pins and U8's CS are therefore on the shared MISO net. The MCU's third chip-select net NET0019 (ESP32 GPIO6) is not present anywhere on the thermocouple sheet, leaving GPIO6 unconnected while U8's ~{CS} rides the MISO line.
anomalies.expected: Per the specification each MAX31855 must have its own independent chip-select: '~{CS} (pin 6) on U2/U3/U4 goes to separate nets CS0/CS1/CS2, driven by ESP32 GPIO4/GPIO6/GPIO7 respectively.' U8's ~{CS} should therefore be on its own net NET0019 (ESP32 GPIO6), not on the shared MISO net.

evidence.quote: Each chip has its own independent chip-select: ~{CS} (pin 6) on U2/U3/U4 goes to separate nets CS0/CS1/CS2, driven by ESP32 GPIO4/GPIO6/GPIO7 respectively.
thermocouples.kicad_sch, U8 MAX31855KASA: SCK (5) -> NET0010, SO (7) -> NET0015, ~{CS} (6) -> NET0015

anomalies.impact: The second thermocouple zone can no longer be addressed independently; its ~{CS} follows the MISO line, so any device driving MISO also selects U8, corrupting all three SPI reads. The firmware will likely report a thermocouple fault for that zone and abort a run.

anomalies.observed: On mcu.kicad_sch the ESP32-C3-MINI-1 (U5) shows the same net label NET0015 on two adjacent GPIO pins (the pins labelled GPIO9 and GPIO10), i.e. both are connected to the shared SPI MISO net.
anomalies.expected: Only one pin should carry MISO (the spec places SPI2 MISO on GPIO10, SCK on GPIO5). A second GPIO should not be tied onto the MISO net.

evidence.quote: SPI2 configured at 60 MHz, mode 0, with sck on GPIO5 and miso on GPIO10
mcu.kicad_sch, U5 ESP32-C3-MINI-1: GPIO9 -> NET0015, GPIO10 -> NET0015

anomalies.impact: Two ESP32 GPIOs are shorted together on the MISO net, so the second GPIO cannot be used for its intended function (fan tach / LED data) and may contend with the SPI bus.

parsed.summary: The thermocouple sheet shows the middle MAX31855's chip-select wired onto the shared MISO net instead of its own CS line, contradicting the specification's three independent chip-selects; the MCU sheet additionally appears to tie GPIO9 and GPIO10 to the same MISO net. The chip-select/MISO short is the clearest deviation and would break independent thermocouple reads.
